open_obligations: Check whether the experimental design can test debate as proposed.
Do not treat the proof-of-concept chat result as evidence for debate.

Note the setting difference: Irving et al. propose debate as a method for training agents via self play with a human judge, and the abstract's one reported experiment is on MNIST with a sparse classifier as judge; Bowman et al.'s experimental design and proof-of-concept experiment have human participants interact with an unreliable large-language-model dialog assistant through chat on MMLU and time-limited QuALITY, and that abstract describes no training.
out.other_title: AI safety via debate (zero-sum debate game)
out.rationale: One abstract defines scalable oversight and an experimental design; the other proposes debate as a way to judge tasks too hard for direct human judgement. The scalable-oversight abstract treats the problem of supervising systems that potentially outperform us and how to study it empirically, which bears on the problem the debate abstract states, that asking humans to judge during training can fail if the task is too complicated for a human to directly judge, so ADDRESSES. The link does not claim that debate solves scalable oversight.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: possible bearing of the scalable-oversight framing and its experimental design on the problem the debate abstract states, that human judgement can fail when a task is too complicated for a human to directly judge
